name: speculation-rules
notes: Adapter-authoring probe 2026-09-08: inspected the official WordPress.org Speculative Loading 1.7.0 artifact (SHA-256 0006fda65ee5bd7c9f76f857af2ce4bcc1e82e47834bc8e3fca341af7c47b4c4). Its seven PHP files declare exactly one persistent row: option plsr_speculation_rules. Measured on WP 7.1: no post type, no taxonomy, no post/term/user meta, no custom table, no transient, no cron event, no site/network option, no shortcode, no widget, no block. uninstall.php deletes that one option and nothing else, so the adapter's ownership and the plugin's own teardown agree exactly.

settings.php plsr_sanitize_setting() seals the key set: array_intersect_key(array_merge($default, $input), $default) against plsr_get_setting_default()'s three keys, then clamps each value to plsr_get_mode_labels()/plsr_get_eagerness_labels()/plsr_get_authentication_labels(). Measured through the native path (update_option runs the registered sanitize_option_plsr_speculation_rules callback): an undeclared sibling key was dropped and an out-of-enum eagerness fell back to 'moderate', leaving exactly a:3:{s:4:"mode";...s:9:"eagerness";...s:14:"authentication";...}. closed_sub_keys therefore states a closure the plugin itself enforces — a fourth key in a future release aborts capture loudly instead of riding along unclassified.

All three sub-keys are site-builder choices constrained to word enums. None is an entity id, URL, secret, cache marker or version stamp, so the capsule withholds nothing and declares no lint_ok, no ref, no plain_data and no allow_secret.

The option is ABSENT on a fresh install (measured: no wp_options row until the first save) and register_setting()'s 'default' plus plsr_sanitize_setting()'s non-array fallback both resolve that absence to prerender/moderate/logged_out. Absence and a stored default row are therefore behaviourally identical by the plugin's own doubled guarantee. The interpreter completes that absence from the plugin's own plsr_get_setting_default() at capture time so an unsaved source still converges a diverged target, and absent_autoload declares the exact insertion storage ('auto' on WP 7.1) the engine refuses to guess.

1.6.0 (SHA-256 55d508085e295534f7592f9603a0603f727cdb3225a3d64c47a0466847e61ad2) carries a byte-identical option surface and identical defaults. The certified window therefore has to refuse it on the declared range alone, with no incidental schema difference to lean on — which is what tests/certify/version-matrix.sh asserts.
